drafts.title: Reduce harsh ride on broken pavement so rough roads feel composed
drafts.description: When driving on broken or uneven pavement, customers experience noticeably less sharp vibrations and jolts — the car feels composed and comfortable rather than harsh.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized broken‑pavement route, a representative user panel (n≥30) rates perceived ride harshness at least 25% better (lower) than the current test vehicle median score; objective ride harshness events (measured on the same route) are reduced by at least 30%.
assumptions: A standardized broken‑pavement route and repeatable ride‑comfort scoring protocol are available for comparison.
Suspension and chassis tuning improvements (software + hardware) can be implemented within the successor program timeline.
uncertainties: Exact baseline performance of the current test vehicle must be defined before final targets are validated.
Perceived comfort is partly subjective; panel composition and test conditions will affect measured improvement.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise on highways above 70 mph
drafts.description: At highway speeds customers hear less wind noise so conversations and audio are not disturbed when driving above 70 mph.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Interior A‑weighted SPL at the driver ear position is ≤68 dB(A) at 75 mph on a standardized highway track (window closed, vents off) and subjective annoyance rating from a user panel (n≥20) is reduced by at least 20% versus current test vehicle.
assumptions: Standardized test track and microphone placement are used for repeatable measurements.
Improvements can be achieved through aero tuning, sealing and trim optimizations within the successor timeline.
uncertainties: Actual baseline loudness and limiting factors (mirrors, seals, glass) must be confirmed during development.

drafts.title: Make lane keeping assist steer smoothly in curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When using lane keeping assist on highways customers feel smooth, predictable steering assistance in curves and do not experience sudden or startling steering corrections.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a set of representative highway curve scenarios (speeds 50–75 mph), abrupt steering assist interventions occur in fewer than 2 events per 100 miles of combined test driving; driver‑initiated overrides attributable to unexpected steering inputs occur ≤1 per 200 miles.
assumptions: Representative test routes with repeated curve segments are defined to detect and count abrupt interventions.
Vehicle is operating within normal lane keeping operating conditions (good lane markings, dry road).
uncertainties: Driver perception of 'abrupt' varies; the chosen test thresholds must be validated with a user panel.
Extreme environmental conditions or degraded lane markings may increase intervention frequency.

drafts.title: Help drivers find compatible fast chargers quickly and confidently on trips
drafts.description: When planning or driving a long trip customers are guided to fast chargers that are compatible with their vehicle and receive clear compatibility and availability information so searching is fast and not confusing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For at least 90% of long‑distance trips (>100 miles) within the U.S. the vehicle navigation identifies compatible fast chargers and presents compatibility, connector type and predicted availability; a compatible charger and route option is provided to the driver within 30 seconds or 3 interactions on the vehicle UI.
assumptions: Access to up‑to‑date charger metadata (connector type, power, network, real‑time availability) is available via partners or aggregators.
Back‑end integrations and real‑time data feeds can be implemented for the successor vehicle.
uncertainties: Coverage and data quality vary by region and network; initial rollout may have gaps in some rural areas.
Different third‑party networks may expose data at different levels of detail or latency.

drafts.title: Make the charge port indicator show charging state clearly at a glance
drafts.description: When charging, customers can see the charge status from a short distance without opening apps — the charge port indicator clearly communicates charging, fully charged and error states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Charge port indicator uses distinct visible signals that can be perceived from 2 meters in daylight (and at typical angles) and unambiguously indicate at least 'charging', 'complete' and 'error' states in a single glance.
assumptions: Indicator visibility in daylight is achievable through hardware placement and signal design refinements.
User testing will validate the color/flash schemes for color‑blind accessibility and clarity.
uncertainties: Exact illumination and visibility will depend on port placement and surrounding geometry.
Local regulations may constrain colors or signals used for external indicators.

uncertainties: Level 3 approval depends on evolving national regulations and authorities.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request — outside product requirement scope and dependent on external type‑approval processes.

drafts.title: Customer request for 600–700 mile real‑world range
drafts.description: Customers explicitly ask for a real‑world range of at least 600 (or 700) miles on one tank or charge.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a customer engineering/target request for a specific range value (600–700 miles); treated as an engineering specification rather than a direct user‑interaction requirement.
assumptions: Achieving 600–700 miles depends on powertrain selection (ICE, hybrid, or very large battery) and is subject to feasibility and regulatory constraints.
uncertainties: Real‑world range depends on driving patterns, speed, environmental conditions and vehicle configuration; feasibility within a successor program must be evaluated.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific numeric range target is an engineering/product strategy decision and thus out of scope for a customer‑facing requirement draft.
